nodes.summary: For $n$ transactions, numbered $0, \dots, n-1$, and a type $X$ of data items, an action of a locked schedule is one of three kinds: a read or write operation; a lock request, in which a transaction $t$ acquires a lock on an item $x \in X$ in a lock mode $m$ (shared or exclusive); or a release, in which a transaction $t$ releases its lock on an item $x \in X$.
nodes.title: Action of a locked schedule

nodes.summary: If the reads and writes of a locked schedule are distinct, are covered by locks, and the schedule is legal and strict two-phase, then its reads and writes form a conflict-serializable schedule.
nodes.title: Strict two-phase locking theorem

nodes.summary: If the reads and writes of a locked schedule are distinct, are covered by locks, and the schedule is legal and two-phase, then its reads and writes form a conflict-serializable schedule.
nodes.title: The two-phase locking theorem

nodes.summary: A lock mode $m'$ covers a lock mode $m$ when a lock in mode $m'$ permits what a lock in mode $m$ permits: an exclusive lock covers both modes, and a shared lock covers only the shared mode.
nodes.title: Lock mode coverage

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a locked schedule, $t$ a transaction, $x$ a data item, $m$ a lock mode and $p$ a natural number. Transaction $t$ holds a lock on $x$ covering mode $m$ just before position $p$ of $s$ when there is a position $q < p$ at which $s$ has a lock request by $t$ on $x$ in some mode $m'$ that covers $m$, and for no position $r$ with $q < r < p$ is the action of $s$ at $r$ a release of $x$ by $t$.
nodes.title: Holding a lock

nodes.summary: For a transaction $t$, this Boolean test on the actions of a locked schedule returns true exactly when the action is a release by $t$ of its lock on some item.
nodes.title: Release test

nodes.summary: A locked schedule $s$ is legal just before position $p$ when, for every data item $x$, all distinct transactions $t \ne t'$ and all lock modes $m$, $m'$: if $t$ holds a lock on $x$ covering $m$ and $t'$ holds a lock on $x$ covering $m'$ just before position $p$ of $s$, then $m$ and $m'$ are both the shared mode. In words, two transactions do not both hold locks on the same item unless both locks are shared.
nodes.title: Lock compatibility at a point

nodes.summary: A locked schedule $s$ of length $\ell$ is legal when it satisfies lock compatibility at every point $p \le \ell$: just before position $p$, no two distinct transactions both hold locks on the same item unless both locks are shared.
nodes.title: Legal locked schedule

nodes.summary: A lock is held in one of two modes: shared (a read lock) or exclusive (a write lock).
nodes.title: Lock mode

nodes.summary: The list of data items locked in a locked schedule $s$: for each lock request of $s$, in order, the item it locks, so an item appears once for each lock request on it.
nodes.title: Locked items

nodes.summary: For a locked schedule $s$ and a position $p$: if $s$ has at position $p$ a read or write $o$ by transaction $t$ on item $x$, then just before position $p$ transaction $t$ holds a lock on $x$ whose mode covers the mode $o$ requires (shared for a read, exclusive for a write; an exclusive lock covers both modes). If position $p$ holds a lock request or a release, or lies beyond the end of $s$, the condition holds…
nodes.title: Lock coverage at a position

nodes.summary: A locked schedule $s$ is covered by locks when every read or write is protected by a lock of its transaction: whenever $s$ has at position $p$ a read or write $o$ by transaction $t$ on item $x$, just before position $p$ transaction $t$ holds a lock on $x$ (acquired at an earlier position and not released since) whose mode covers the mode $o$ requires, namely shared for a read and exclusive for a write; an exclusive…
nodes.title: Schedules covered by locks

nodes.summary: The lock mode an access requires: shared for a read, exclusive for a write.
nodes.title: Lock mode required by an access

nodes.summary: For a locked schedule $s$, the schedule of reads and writes of $s$: its reads and writes in order, with the lock requests and releases erased.
nodes.title: Reads and writes of a locked schedule

nodes.summary: For a locked schedule $s$ and a position $q$: if $s$ has at position $q$ a lock request (in either mode) by transaction $t$ on item $x$, then there is a position $r$ with $q < r$ and $r$ less than the length of $s$ at which $s$ has a release by $t$ of $x$. If position $q$ holds a read, a write or a release, or lies beyond the end of $s$, the condition holds trivially.
nodes.title: Release of the lock requested at a position

nodes.summary: A locked schedule $s$ releases its locks when every lock request is followed by a matching release: whenever $s$ has at position $q$ a lock request (in either mode) by transaction $t$ on item $x$, there is a position $r > q$ at which $s$ has a release by $t$ of $x$.
nodes.title: Schedules that release every lock

nodes.summary: For a locked schedule $s$ and positions $p$ and $q$: if $s$ has at position $p$ a release by transaction $t$ of item $x$, just before position $p$ transaction $t$ holds an exclusive lock on $x$, and $s$ has at position $q$ a read or write by $t$, then $q < p$. For every other pair of positions, including positions beyond the end of $s$, the condition holds trivially.
nodes.title: Strictness at a pair of positions

nodes.summary: A locked schedule $s$ is strict two-phase when it is two-phase and every transaction releases its exclusive locks only after its last read or write: whenever $s$ has at position $p$ a release by transaction $t$ of item $x$ and just before position $p$ transaction $t$ holds an exclusive lock on $x$, every read or write of $t$ in $s$ occurs at a position before $p$.
nodes.title: Strict two-phase schedules

nodes.summary: For a locked schedule $s$ and positions $p$ and $q$: if $s$ has at position $p$ a release by transaction $t$ and at position $q$ a lock request by the same transaction $t$, then $q < p$. For every other pair of positions, including positions beyond the end of $s$, the condition holds trivially.
nodes.title: Two-phase condition at a pair of positions

nodes.summary: A locked schedule $s$ is two-phase when every lock request of a transaction precedes every release of that transaction: whenever $s$ has at position $p$ a release by transaction $t$ and at position $q$ a lock request by $t$ (on any items, in any mode), then $q < p$.
nodes.title: Two-phase schedules

nodes.summary: A locked schedule $s$ (a list of reads, writes, lock requests and lock releases of transactions) is well formed when its accesses are covered by locks and it releases its locks: every read or write in $s$ is preceded by a lock request of its own transaction on its item, in a mode covering the access (shared or exclusive for a read, exclusive for a write), with no release of that item by that transaction in between;…
nodes.title: Well-formed locked schedules

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
